candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items), within Physiological Integrity; this item tests supportive postoperative respiratory care, mobility, pain control, and comfort measures that promote effective breathing and recovery.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Comfort-supportive respiratory care and multimodal postoperative pulmonary-complication prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Use incentive spirometry, when ordered for postoperative care, as an adjunct within a multimodal lung-expansion strategy rather than as a stand-alone replacement for deep breathing, coughing, mobilization, and adequate analgesia.

options.A: Use incentive spirometry as one component of care along with deep-breathing techniques, directed coughing, early mobilization, and adequate pain control
options.B: Use incentive spirometry alone as the routine prophylactic intervention and omit other postoperative pulmonary measures
options.C: Keep the client on bed rest so incentive spirometry can replace early mobilization
options.D: Avoid deep-breathing exercises because they provide no comparable postoperative benefit

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The AARC incentive-spirometry guideline states that incentive spirometry alone is not recommended for routine preoperative or postoperative prevention of pulmonary complications. When incentive spirometry is used, AARC recommends combining it with deep-breathing techniques, directed coughing, early mobilization, and optimal analgesia. The guideline also notes that deep-breathing exercises may provide similar benefit to incentive spirometry in the perioperative setting. B incorrectly treats incentive spirometry as a stand-alone routine prophylaxis. C contradicts the recommendation for early mobilization. D contradicts the guideline's recognition of deep-breathing benefit.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current AARC guideline resources directly support incentive spirometry only as part of a broader postoperative respiratory-care strategy and reject routine stand-alone prophylactic use.
candidate.source_document_title: Incentive Spirometry: 2011 — AARC Clinical Practice Guideline; AARC Clinical Practice Guideline: Effectiveness of Nonpharmacologic Airway Clearance Therapies in Hospitalized Patients
candidate.source_locator: AARC 'Incentive Spirometry: 2011' → Recommendations 14.1–14.5: incentive spirometry alone is not recommended for routine pre/postoperative prevention; when used, combine with deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobilization, and optimal analgesia; deep-breathing exercises may provide the same perioperative benefit; routine use to prevent atelectasis after upper-abdominal surgery or CABG is not recommended. AARC guideline index → Incentive Spirometry (2011) remains listed under Expert Panel Reference-Based Guidelines. 2013 nonpharmacologic airway-clearance guideline → postoperative recommendations: routine prophylactic incentive spirometry is not recommended; early mobility/ambulation is recommended.
candidate.source_version_date: Incentive Spirometry guideline published 2011 and still listed by AARC in 2026 as an Expert Panel Reference-Based Guideline, not retired; postoperative airway-clearance guideline published 2013 and current on AARC guideline resources at access 2026-08-18
